value.rationale: The finite-N covariance of two actual sites is a natural measure of shared population/wealth risk under independent catastrophes and mean-field redistribution. Its exact redistribution-invariant critical surface is not an arbitrary normalization: at m=r/2, increasing redistribution changes variance and Pearson correlation but cannot change unstandardized covariance. A complete if-and-only-if finite-size second-moment frontier quantifies when migration rescues finite stationary variability, with a previously unreported square-root crossover.
